feedback:
Approved because one action run remains and a revise round would leave no run for the race. The candidate differs from the iteration 3 best (score 517.2) only in controller.base_speed, 1.2 to 1.1. kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0, line_loss 'last_direction' and geometry are unchanged. Evidence from iteration 3: the oval finished 19 of 20 runs with max_error 0.021. The s-bend finished 6 of 20 with max_error 0.054, and the slalom finished 0 of 20 with max_error 0.064 and one line-loss event per run. rms_error stayed low (0.008 to 0.019), so the failures are edge excursions on bends, not poor average tracking. steering_oscillation was 0.37 on the s-bend, 0.26 on the oval and 0.20 on the slalom. The kd rule has already been applied (kd 0.8). The remaining lever is speed, and the candidate is a one-parameter test of it. I make no prediction of how this candidate will perform.

How to use the telemetry in the next iteration. If the slalom max_error falls below 0.06 and its line_loss_events drop toward 0.5 or less, speed was the limit, so hold base_speed near 1.1. If the slalom still ends off track at 1.1, the next change is sensor geometry: widen the sensor spread to x near plus or minus 0.03 m, keeping the other fields fixed. If s-bend completion_time rises above 3 s, do not raise base_speed again, because the time limit is then binding.
requested_changes: If the slalom still ends off track with max_error at or above 0.06 at base_speed 1.1, keep controller.base_speed at 1.1 and change geometry.sensor_positions to a wider spread (x near -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m), since iteration 3 slalom max_error was 0.064 and the sensor spread is untested.

If slalom and s-bend max_error drop below 0.06 at base_speed 1.1 but s-bend completion_time exceeds 3 s, hold controller.base_speed at 1.1 or move it to 1.15, not lower, since iteration 3 s-bend mean finish time was 2.56 s at base_speed 1.2.
If steering_oscillation remains near 0.37 on the s-bend with kd 0.8, do not raise kd further without a race result; test controller.kd 0.9 only after speed and geometry have been isolated.
